Auterion, a leading provider of autonomous systems software for defence, has raised $130 million in Series B funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners.
The investment will accelerate the scale-up of the company’s AuterionOS platform and Nemyx defence system, which turns individual drones into coordinated swarms across air, land and sea domains.
Lorenz Meier, Founder and CEO of Auterion, said: “The future of warfare is software-defined, unmanned, and at scale. Auterion’s customers are taking the lessons from Ukraine and applying them to deploying drone swarms. Decisive advantage on the battlefield won’t be achieved by individual drones – it’ll be achieved by autonomous mass.
The company’s Skynode X system integrates autopilot, mission computer, AI-powered autonomy, secure communications and edge computing, allowing drones to complete missions even under GPS and video jamming. Tested in combat, this technology is already in use on the battlefield.
Auterion’s systems are deployed in Ukraine, where under a Pentagon contract the company is delivering tens of thousands of AI “strike kits” to forces in the field. This represents the largest deployment of autonomous technology in the West to date, scaling up from thousands to tens of thousands of units.

European Strategic Autonomy Is an Illusion
European countries possess few aircraft capable of collecting signals intelligence (SIGINT) and electronic intelligence (ELINT); most of their aircraft that have these capabilities are American-made.
Moreover, the countries that operate the largest proportion of these platforms—Turkey and the United Kingdom—are members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) but not of the European Union (EU).
Europe also lacks high-end kinetic combat and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) drones.
Currently, the European drone market is dominated by General Atomics, a U.S. company, while Turkey is the continent’s newest major drone supplier. NATO is also heavily dependent on the United States for space assets.
At the same time, Washington provides the alliance with the majority of its large tanker and transport fleets for aerial refueling and strategic air mobility. These deficiencies in strategic enablers leave Europe with a dearth of sovereign military action capabilities.
The European Commission’s most recent defense assessment, the Joint White Paper for European Defense Readiness 2030, lists seven capability gaps it must close: space assets, air and missile defense, cyber and electronic warfare, drones and anti-drone systems, military mobility, artillery systems, and strategic enablers.

candidates.source_name: Jindal Drilling Receives 3-Year ONGC Award For Rig Jindal Pioneer At ₹45.83 Lakh Daily
candidates.snippet:
Jindal Drilling has received a 3-year Notification of Award from ONGC for its jack-up rig, Jindal Pioneer, at an Effective Day Rate of ₹45.83 lakh. Currently under refurbishment, the rig is scheduled to commence operations in Q3 FY27, bolstering the company's long-term revenue visibility.
Author Image
Sahi Markets
SAHI Perspective
The award of this contract is a major milestone for Jindal Drilling. It validates the strategic acquisition of the Jindal Pioneer jack-up rig in March 2025 for USD 75 million. By securing a day rate of ₹45.83 lakh (approx.
Market Implications
The long-term contract ensures steady operating cash flows from FY27 through FY30. For the offshore drilling sector, this award signals robust domestic exploration and production capex by state-owned players like ONGC. Additionally, this supports high day rates across the Indian offshore market.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bullish
The 3-year charter secures high-margin contract backlog for Jindal Pioneer at a lucrative EDR of ₹45.83 lakh. While operations commence in Q3 FY27, this significantly enhances long-term valuation metrics and cash flow predictability.
Overweight: Oil Drilling & Exploration Services, Oilfield Equipment
Trigger Factors:
* Commencement of rig operations in Q3 FY27.
* Successful completion of current refurbishment in UAE.
* Stability in global Brent crude prices supporting ONGC's drilling capex.
  Time Horizon: Medium-term (3-12 months)
